| SurveyGen | 35.84% citation accuracy |

sentences carried citations — statistically indistinguishable.** The presence of
a citation carries almost no information. That is the justification for

`requirements.txt` written at the repo root — 31 entries, parses under pip, and every floor is satisfied by your current environment (Python 3.14.6).

**How I built it:** the repo already declares deps in `pyproject.toml` as phase-grouped extras, so I mirrored that structure section by section with identical floors, rather than inventing a second source of truth. A header comment says so explicitly — change one, change both.

**Four things I added beyond `pyproject.toml`**, all direct module-level or function-local imports the project relies on but only gets transitively today:

| package | why | where |
|---|---|---|
| `numpy>=1.26` | module-level import | `agents/verifier.py`, `tools/reranker.py` |
| `huggingface-hub>=0.23` | `hf_hub_download` | `verify/scifact_pairs.py`, `eval/scireviewgen.py` |
| `torch>=2.2` | ONNX export / checkpoint eval | `verify/export_onnx.py`, `rerank/export_onnx.py` |
| `scipy>=1.11` | `kendalltau` | `rerank/export_onnx.py` |

They all arrive with `sentence-transformers` anyway, so declaring them costs nothing at install time and stops a future dependency change from silently breaking those modules.

**Two judgment calls worth a look:**

- I included the `db` extra (`sqlalchemy`, `psycopg[binary]`) even though T-625 says the pipeline must run with no database. Installing them doesn't violate that — nothing on the core path imports `sqlalchemy`, and an empty `DATABASE_URL` still disables the registry. The comment in the file states this.
- The last line is `-e .`, so one command gives you a working `researchgpt` CLI (the `src/` layout needs it). If you'd rather the file be dependencies-only, delete that line — it's flagged with a comment.

No LLM vendor SDKs are listed because there aren't any: `core/llm.py` calls Groq and Gemini over raw `httpx`. The frontend keeps its own deps in `frontend/package.json`, untouched.

I didn't run a full `pip install -r requirements.txt` to confirm end-to-end resolution — that would re-resolve ~30 packages against PyPI. The static checks (parse + floor satisfaction against your working env) both pass; say the word if you want the real install run.
